subject: Physics
source: Phase F · FEAT-PF1 — author-original scaffold rows for the highest-volume AQA Y10 physics spec points (8463).

sentenceFrames: I will use the equation KE = ½ × m × v².
Mass m = ______ kg. Velocity v = ______ m/s.

wordBank.definition: the energy an object has because it is moving
the amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms
speed in a stated direction, measured in metres per second

stepLadder: Write down the equation KE = ½mv².
Identify the mass and the velocity from the question.
Make sure both are in SI units (kg and m/s).
Substitute numbers into the equation, keeping the velocity squared bracketed.
Calculate and write the answer with the unit (joules).
Sense-check: KE doubles if mass doubles, but quadruples if velocity doubles.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting the ½ at the start.
Mixing units (e.g. mass in grams, expecting an answer in joules).
rows.visualAidHint: Always write the equation first, then substitute. Boxes around each substituted value reduce arithmetic mistakes.

sentenceFrames: I will use Ohm's law: V = I × R.

wordBank.definition: the energy transferred per unit charge, measured in volts
the rate of flow of charge, measured in amps
the opposition to current flow, measured in ohms (Ω)
a component whose resistance stays constant; current is proportional to potential difference

stepLadder: Identify which of V, I, R you are asked to find.
Rearrange the equation for that quantity (R = V/I or I = V/R).
Calculate and give the answer with the correct unit.
commonPitfalls: Mixing up which letter stands for which quantity.
Wrong rearrangement (e.g. R = I × V instead of R = V/I).
Forgetting the unit in the answer (V, A or Ω).
rows.visualAidHint: An Ohm's law triangle (V on top, I and R on bottom) reminds pupils which quantity to divide or multiply.

wordBank.definition: mass per unit volume; ρ = m/V
the amount of matter in an object, measured in g or kg
the space an object takes up, measured in cm³ or m³

stepLadder: Calculate the volume of the cuboid (length × width × height).
Make sure the units of mass and volume match (g & cm³ or kg & m³).
Give the answer with the correct unit (g/cm³ or kg/m³).
Compare with water (1 g/cm³) to sense-check.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting the unit on the answer.
